issues.description: The problem statement and template expect a method named swiftExperienceDescription() on Developer, and Client.swift calls swiftExperienceDescription(), but the solution defines and uses a differently named method getExperienceDescription(). This name/signature mismatch between the Developer implementation and Client usage will cause a compile-time error and confuses students about the required method name.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method name across all artifacts. Either rename getExperienceDescription() in Sources/DeveloperLib/Developer.swift to swiftExperienceDescription() and call that in the initializer, or add a swiftExperienceDescription() wrapper that returns getExperienceDescription(). Ensure Client.swift and the template refer to the same method name.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template require a Developer instance method named swiftExperienceDescription(), but the solution's implementation defines and calls a method named getExperienceDescription(). This naming divergence for the same conceptual operation (producing a printable Swift experience description) creates a mapping mismatch: students reading the solution may not see the expected method name from the exercise prompt/template and could be confused about which identifier to implement or call.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a consistent method name across all artifacts. Rename the solution method getExperienceDescription() to swiftExperienceDescription(), and update all internal calls (e.g. in the initializer and any callers) to call swiftExperienceDescription(). Alternatively, change the template and problem to reference getExperienceDescription(), but prefer aligning the solution to the problem/template name to avoid confusing students.
